name: example_sop_v0
note: EXAMPLE operating procedures written for a first RAG test. Not an authoritative SOP. General rules are always retrieved; conditional rules are retrieved from observable symptoms only (no disturbance identity).

rules.title: Normal operation: hold
rules.text: If no alarm is active, no protection override is active, reactor pressure is below 2800 kPa and not rising faster than 20 kPa/h, and no controller MV command is saturated at 0 % or 100 %, HOLD. The Mode-1 setpoints are the economically optimized operating point; do not move any setpoint without a specific abnormal symptom.

rules.title: Change discipline
rules.text: Change at most one or two setpoints per decision and in small steps (production_rate at most 5 % of its initial value, other setpoints at most 2 %). After a change, wait at least 1 h (4 decisions) to see its effect before changing the same setpoint again, unless an alarm appears or worsens.

rules.title: Reactor pressure setpoint and cost
rules.text: Keep the reactor_pressure setpoint at its initial value (about 2705 kPa). A lower reactor pressure raises operating cost (more purge loss and compressor work). Lower it only when measured pressure approaches 2850 kPa and production cuts have not stopped the rise.

rules.title: Level setpoints are inventory buffers
rules.text: Reactor (75 %), separator (50 %) and stripper (50 %) level setpoints are inventory buffers with no steady-state economic benefit. Keep them at their initial values. Never set the separator or stripper level setpoint below 40 %: low levels remove the buffer against upsets and risk the 0 % trip.

rules.title: Composition and temperature setpoints
rules.text: Keep ya, yac and reactor_temperature setpoints at their initial values unless a reactor temperature alarm is active or reactor-feed composition has drifted for more than 1 h.

rules.title: High or rising reactor pressure
rules.trigger: reactor pressure > 2800 kPa and rising, or a reactor pressure alarm, or the high-pressure override active
rules.text: Reduce the production_rate setpoint by 5 % of its initial value. If pressure is still rising after 1 h, reduce by another 5 %. Do not change level, temperature or composition setpoints for this symptom. Lowering production is the primary lever for reactor pressure.

rules.title: Loss of A feed
rules.trigger: A feed flow near zero while the A feed valve command is at 100 %
rules.text: The A feed is lost. Reactor pressure will rise over the next several hours. Reduce the production_rate setpoint early, by 10-15 % of its initial value, before pressure alarms appear. Hold all other setpoints.

rules.title: Restore production
rules.trigger: production_rate setpoint below its initial value
rules.text: When reactor pressure is below 2750 kPa and stable for 2 h with no alarm and no override, raise production_rate back toward its initial value in steps of 5 %. Otherwise hold the reduced production.
